html:
Closer Economic Relations (CER) is the free trade agreement between Australia and New Zealand. It came into force on 1 January 1983 and is often called one of the most complete trade deals in the world.

The push came from loss. When Britain joined the European Economic Community in 1973, New Zealand and Australian farmers lost much of their old British market, and the two neighbours looked to each other. An older and weaker deal of 1965 was replaced by CER, agreed by the governments of Malcolm Fraser and Robert Muldoon.

  • All tariffs and quotas on goods between the two were gone by 1990.
  • Trade in services was added in 1988.
  • Food standards, business law and other rules were slowly lined up.

Together with the Trans-Tasman Travel Arrangement, which lets citizens of each country live and work in the other, CER made the two economies close to a single market. It became a model for later regional deals such as the ASEAN Free Trade Area.
